text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: spike in 5xx and gateway timeouts hitting /v1/chat.generate. Alerts from autoscaler + gateway showing increased 502/504 across eu-central-1 and ap-southeast-1. Paging @liz_oncall.

liz_oncall: I'm here. quick snapshot of customer impact pls.

sara_prod: two enterprise customers (marketplaces) report elevated errors and session drops. eu-central ~30% error rate for some endpoints in last 12m; apac ~12%. Users see either 502 or long TTFB > 8s.

raj_sre: pulling logs from model-runner in eu-central-1. running `kubectl -n inference logs deploy/model-runner -c runner --since=15m | sed -n '1,200p'`

raj_sre: log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-15T22:07:11Z] runner: request id=xyz789 model=llama-compact kernel_fp=quant_attn ERROR: segfault in cu_kernel.cu:attn_forward+0x3f
[2026-03-15T22:07:11Z] cuda: driver report OOM on stream 2 before alloc 800MB
[2026-03-15T22:07:12Z] convo: client retry -> gateway returned 504
[2026-03-15T22:07:12Z] runner: healthcheck failing on pod/runner-7fb6 (oom)
```

cheng_runtime: looks like attention kernel OOB write causing SIGSEGV then OOM cascade. noticed similar once when kv-cache growth exceeded node local allocator threshold.

liz_oncall: mitigation options now? prioritize keeping customers running and capturing repro.

raj_sre: immediate actions in progress: 1) route long-context & streaming clients off eu-central -> move to us-east-1 and to variant `fp16-stable` (no quant-attn); 2) lower per-request kv-cache cap via config (KVCACHE_MAX_TOKENS=1_000_000) to limit memory growth; 3) set runtime env `REDWOOD_DISABLE_PREFETCH=1` to reduce parallel allocations. commands: `./ops/route-util set-prefs --region eu-central-1 --shift 65 --target us-east-1 --variant fp16-stable`

ops_bot: routing action accepted  shift 65% eu-central-1 -> us-east-1 (variant=fp16-stable)  performed by raj_sre

tessa_cs: contacting affected accounts now. posting interim note that we are mitigating and will follow up with timeline & RCA.

raj_sre: also toggling autoscaler min replicas + adding hot nodes in us-east-1: `kubectl scale deploy/model-runner --replicas=40 -n inference` to absorb shifted traffic.

cheng_runtime: please pause any kernel binary swaps. we only want logging-enabled roll restarts for pods in eu-central. set `REDWOOD_ATTN_DEBUG=1` to capture bounds-check info.

liz_oncall: are we collecting minidumps / cores? we need full GPU dumps + the runtime binary SHA.

raj_sre: enabled coredump + gpu-minidump upload to s3://redwood-incidents/INF-2026-4399/; collecting `nvidia-smi dmon` traces as well.

cheng_runtime: initial binary backtrace pulled from one core: `quant_attn.cu:line 520` shows write outside of `kv_idx` when seq_len > 6k. attaching trace to the ticket.

liz_oncall: temp workaround for clients: route streaming & long seq to `fp16-stable`, keep short chat on primary. also reduce max_batch_tokens to 256 to avoid big accumulator allocations.

raj_sre: applied `MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=256` cluster-wide for inference runtime. monitoring.

ops_bot: config change applied cluster-wide by raj_sre.

tessa_cs: logged all impacted sessions and escalated to CSMs; offering credits and prolonged SLA checks.

liz_oncall: status check 10m after mitigations?

raj_sre: metrics: eu-central 5xx dropped from ~30% -> 11% after routing + kvcap + batch cap. apac from ~12% -> 4%. error spike tails still present on a small subset (~6 pods) where reproducer traces kept them alive for debugging. overall traffic stability improving.

cheng_runtime: starting reproducer on p4d with seq=8192 steps, quant path enabled and kvcap toggles to confirm off-by-one. will capture nvprof and address sanitizer on CPU side for kernel launcher.

liz_oncall: handoff to eng-runtime for deeper triage. owners: cheng_runtime, raj_sre. oncall remains as incident lead and will coordinate customer updates. please post hourly.

cheng_runtime: reproduced locally: reproducer fails when combined: quantized kernel + streaming prefetch + kv-cache expanding beyond 1.2M tokens. immediate code fix candidate: add bounds check in attention assembly at index `kidx` and clamp writes. preparing patch + CI.

raj_sre: preserving 35% of eu-central traffic to retain traces until a canary patch is validated. cores + nvprof uploaded to s3 with links in INF-2026-4399.

liz_oncall: summary for the incident doc (to paste into ticket): trigger: elevated 5xx due to SIGSEGV and OOM in quantized attention kernel during long-context inference; impact: partial degradation affecting EU/APAC customers, peak eu-central ~30% 5xx; mitigations: traffic shift to us-east-1 + fp16 fallback, reduced kv-cache cap, disabled prefetch, lowered batch token cap, hot scale up in target region, coredump collection; status: partial mitigation stable (eu-central 5xx ~11%), reproducer confirmed, eng-runtime working on kernel bounds fix.

ops_bot: incident ticket INF-2026-4399 created. Severity: S2. Incident lead: liz_oncall.

tessa_cs: customer comms drafted and queued; waiting on eng ETA for final timeline.

liz_oncall: handoff checklist -> include reproducer cmd, cores location, list of affected pods, routing snapshot, and current metrics. I'll remain incident lead until resolved.

cheng_runtime: pushing experimental patch to `runtime/attn/patch-4399` with additional bounds guards. will canary in us-east-1 with 5% traffic once QA signs off.

raj_sre: once canary is live we'll monitor errors + nvprof traces; if green we'll roll out and then revert routing shift and re-enable prefetch/batching gradually.

incident-bot: NOTE: thread archived when incident status set to resolved.

[end of thread]
